taskTitle: Where ten HTTP header fields are defined

checks.detail: 3 subtasks, read from the schema reply
5 phases had the tools designed for them

finalText:
All ten fields are currently defined by **RFC 9110**, **RFC 9111**, **RFC 6797** or **RFC 8288**. One check is unfinished: no worker could open a status page confirming that none of these four RFCs has itself been obsoleted.

**Caching fields: RFC 9111, "HTTP Caching"** (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html)
- Age: Section 5.1
- Cache-Control: Section 5.2
- Expires: Section 5.3
- The page header says "Obsoletes: 7234", so the older RFC 7234 definitions don't count.

**Semantics fields: RFC 9110, "HTTP Semantics"** (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html)
- Last-Modified: Section 8.8.2
- ETag: Section 8.8.3
- Location: Section 10.2.2
- Retry-After: Section 10.2.3
- Vary: Section 12.5.5
- Its header lists "Obsoletes: 2818, 7230, 7231, 7232, 7233, 7235, 7538, 7615, 7694". That replaces the older definitions in RFC 7231 and RFC 7232.

**Strict-Transport-Security: RFC 6797, Section 6.1** (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6797.html)
- Section 6.1 gives the definition and the syntax rules (ABNF).
- Section 15 only registers the field with IANA, so it is not the defining section.

**Link: RFC 8288, Section 3** (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8288.html)
- Section 3 opens with the definition and the rule `Link = #link-value`.
- The page header says "Obsoletes: 5988", so RFC 5988 doesn't count.

**Limits of the evidence**
- **RFC status not confirmed.** Every status page the workers tried either returned 404 or redirected to the RFC text itself. That covers rfc-editor.org/info/…, the datatracker pages and the IANA field registry.
  - The RFC pages they opened showed no "Obsoleted by" line.
  - A search for anything replacing RFC 9110 found nothing.
  - So the evidence that these four RFCs are still current is indirect.
- **Line breaks in quotes.** Several quoted sentences ran over more than one line on the fetched pages. The workers joined those lines with single spaces, so a strict check on whitespace could flag them.
- No sources disagreed.
